sentiment.rationale: The document shows genuine operational momentum: revenue surged 35% to $22.7B, core loss per share improved from ($2.90) to ($1.24), and free cash flow improved from ($4.3B) to ($0.2B). Management raised the 737 delivery target from ~400 to 'a little better than 400' and expects positive free cash flow in Q4, which is a meaningful forward improvement. However, the structural risk of unresolved certification issues for the 737-7/10 (now pushed to 2026) and the ongoing DOJ non-prosecution agreement charge ($445M) prevent a higher score. Guidance was effectively raised on deliveries and cash flow, but not formally on earnings.

summary.revenue: $22.7 billion, up 35% from $16.9 billion in Q2 2024, primarily reflecting 150 commercial deliveries.
summary.eps: GAAP loss per share of ($0.92) and core loss per share (non-GAAP) of ($1.24), compared to ($2.33) and ($2.90) respectively in Q2 2024.
summary.guidance: Management expects Q3 free cash flow to be 'more or less in line with the second quarter usage' and 'positive free cash flow in the fourth quarter.' 737 deliveries are expected to be 'a little better than the 400' for the full year. 787 deliveries are expected at the high end of the 70-80 range. BCA margins expected to be negative for the year but improving quarter by quarter.
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin was (0.8)% vs (6.5)% in Q2 2024. Core operating margin (non-GAAP) was (1.9)% vs (8.3)% in Q2 2024.
key_risks: 737-7 and 737-10 certification delayed to 2026 due to engine anti-ice solution taking longer than expected.
Potential $700 million one-time payment related to DOJ non-prosecution agreement in Q3.
Ongoing tariff/trade policy uncertainty, particularly with China and USMCA.
Work stoppage risk from a strike affecting ~3,200 employees in St. Louis and St. Charles.
Fixed-price development programs in BDS still represent 15% of revenue and need to be stabilized.
key_opportunities: Strong market demand with backlog of $619 billion, including over 5,900 commercial airplanes.
737 production rate increased to 38/month, with plans to request FAA approval to go to 42/month in coming months.
787 production rate now at 7/month with KPIs all green, positioning for future rate increases.
BDS booked $19B in orders in the quarter, backlog grew to $74B.
Recent trade deals (EU, UK, Japan) expected to reduce tariff impact below the $500M bogey.
Reconciliation Bill increases national defense spending by $150B through FY2029, benefiting Boeing defense programs.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Kelly Ortberg stated 'It's clear our recovery plan is taking hold' and 'We're starting to see real momentum,' while Brian West noted 'free cash flow was better than expectations shared in April.'
